main_text.p: im, ut נְמֵלָה nemelá, formica, נְמָלִים neme-lím, formicæ.
Quædam habent utranq; terminatio-nem plurale, ut, שָׁנָה schaná, annus, שָׁנוֹת schánoth, & שָׁנִים schanim, anni.
Nomina dualitatem significantia faciunt dualem numerum in יִם im, præce-dentē pathah, ut רֶגֶל règhel, pes, רַגְלַיִם raghlájim, ambo pedes.
main_text.head: Declina Adjectiva Anomala, quæ ab aliis pronomina appellantur.
Singularis Numerus.
main_text.p: N. אֲנִי ani & אָנֹכִי anochi, ego. 'i & נִי ni, affixa pronomina dicuntur, eo quod nunquam inueniantur separatim, sed perpetuo fini vocis adhærescant. 'i cum nominibus significat, meus, mea, meum, ut, אָבִי abi, pater meus: נִי ni, cū verbis denotat, me, ut פָּקָדַנִי pekadáni, visitauit me.

page.notes: The Hebrew vowel points are copied as far as they are legible; some may be slightly off. The initial mark before "i" (after "ego.") is printed as a small apostrophe and is copied as such. The "N." opening the paragraph is a printed letter marker. The vowel signs on "ani" and "anochi" are uncertain. The headings are judged from size and type; the second and third are set in italic and roman small type and are given level 3.
